tips.text: Take your medicines exactly as prescribed and keep your next appointment.
Drink enough water, eat balanced meals and aim for 7 to 8 hours of sleep.
Note down any symptoms so you can discuss them at your next visit.
Contact the clinic if your symptoms worsen or new symptoms appear.
Check your blood sugar as advised by your doctor and note the readings to share at your next visit.
Take diabetes medicine or insulin at the same times every day and do not skip doses.
Choose whole grains, vegetables and protein, and limit sugary drinks and sweets.
Check your feet daily for cuts or sores and tell your doctor if they do not heal.
Check your blood pressure at the same time each day and keep a written log.
Reduce salt in your meals and avoid packaged salty snacks.
Take your blood pressure medicine every day, even when you feel well.
Walk briskly for about 30 minutes on most days unless your doctor advises otherwise.
Keep your reliever inhaler with you at all times.
Use your controller inhaler daily as prescribed, even when you have no symptoms.
Avoid known triggers such as dust, smoke and strong smells.
Seek urgent care if you have severe breathlessness that your reliever inhaler does not relieve.
Limit fried and processed foods and eat more fibre such as oats, fruits and vegetables.
Stay active with at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise each week.
Take your cholesterol medicine as prescribed and repeat your lipid test when your doctor advises.
Take your thyroid tablet at the same time every day, as directed by your doctor, usually on an empty stomach.
Get your thyroid blood test (TSH) done on schedule so your dose can be reviewed.
Tell your doctor about unusual tiredness, weight changes or a racing heartbeat.
Avoid sitting for long periods; stand up and stretch every 30 to 45 minutes.
Do the gentle stretches shown by your physiotherapist and avoid lifting heavy weights.
Bend at the knees and keep your back straight when picking things up.
Contact us urgently if you notice leg weakness, numbness or loss of bladder control.
Rest the knee, apply ice for 15 to 20 minutes a few times a day and keep it raised.
Do the strengthening exercises your physiotherapist recommended.
Avoid twisting movements and high-impact activity until your doctor clears you.
Contact the clinic if swelling, redness or pain increases.
Keep a headache diary noting triggers such as poor sleep, skipped meals, stress and screen time.
Keep regular sleep and meal times and drink enough water.
Take your migraine medicine early, at the first sign of an attack, exactly as prescribed.
Rest in a dark, quiet room during an attack.
Drink plenty of fluids and get plenty of rest.
If your fever lasts more than three days or you have trouble breathing, contact us or visit the nearest hospital.
If antibiotics were prescribed, complete the full course.
Keep the wound clean and dry and follow your dressing instructions.
Call us if you notice fever, redness, swelling or discharge at the wound.
Take short walks regularly to support recovery, and avoid heavy lifting until you are cleared.
Take pain medicine only as prescribed.
Gentle low-impact exercise such as walking or swimming helps keep your joints flexible.
A warm compress can ease stiffness, and a cold pack can reduce swelling.
Keeping a healthy weight reduces stress on your joints.
Avoid known triggers and use a mild, fragrance-free soap.
Moisturise your skin regularly and avoid scratching; keep your nails short.
Use any prescribed cream exactly as directed.
Eat smaller, regular meals and avoid spicy and oily food.
Do not lie down for two hours after eating.
Limit tea, coffee, alcohol and smoking.
Take your acid medicine as prescribed, before meals if your doctor advised.
Eat iron-rich foods such as leafy greens, lentils and jaggery, along with vitamin C foods like lemon or amla.
Take iron supplements as prescribed and avoid taking them with tea or coffee.
Repeat your haemoglobin test when your doctor advises.
Take your folic acid, iron and calcium supplements as prescribed.
Attend all scheduled antenatal check-ups and scans.
Contact us right away for bleeding, severe headache, fluid leaking or reduced baby movements.
Keep a regular sleep routine and include light physical activity in your day.
Talk to someone you trust if you feel low, and keep your next appointment.
If you ever feel unsafe or have thoughts of self-harm, call emergency services or a crisis helpline immediately.
Drink plenty of water through the day.
Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
Contact us if you develop fever, back pain or blood in your urine.
